\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{تزیین} \fa{کردن} (tazyin kardan)}{تزیین کردن (tazyin kardan)}]{\fa{تزیین} \fa{کردن} (tazyin kardan) — to decorate}

\label{lesson:FA-C342-tazyin-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a balloon, then the Persian for a candle.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{تزیین} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{تزیین} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{tazyin kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to decorate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{ما} \fa{خانه} \fa{را} \fa{با} \fa{گل} \fa{تزیین} \fa{کردیم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Mâ khâne râ bâ gol tazyin kardim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We decorated the house with flowers.
\end{quote}

Also spelled \fa{تزئین}. Present \emph{tazyin mikonad}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{tazyin} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{tazyīn}, \textquotedblleft{}adornment\textquotedblright{}; EtymDB lists no entry. \emph{kardan} \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tazyin kardan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{tazyin kardan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a balloon, then the Persian for a candle, then say \emph{tazyin kardan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{چراغانی} (cherâghâni)}{چراغانی (cherâghâni)}]{\fa{چراغانی} (cherâghâni) — festive lights, illuminations}

\label{lesson:FA-C342-cheraghani}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a candle, then the Persian for to decorate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{چراغانی}}
\textbf{\fa{چراغانی}} (\emph{cherâghâni}) — \textquotedblleft{}festive lights, illuminations\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{خیابان} \fa{ها} \fa{برای} \fa{جشن} \fa{چراغانی} \fa{بود}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Khiyâbân-hâ barâ-ye jashn cherâghâni bud.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The streets were lit up for the celebration.
\end{quote}

From \emph{cherâgh} \textquotedblleft{}lamp\textquotedblright{}: strings of lights for a festival.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{cherâghâni} is built on \emph{cherâgh} \textquotedblleft{}lamp\textquotedblright{}, a Persian word, with the suffix \emph{-âni}; EtymDB lists no entry.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{آتش} \fa{بازی} (âtash bâzi)}{آتش بازی (âtash bâzi)}]{\fa{آتش} \fa{بازی} (âtash bâzi) — fireworks}

\label{lesson:FA-C342-atash-bazi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to decorate, then the Persian for festive lights.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{آتش} \fa{بازی}}
\textbf{\fa{آتش} \fa{بازی}} (\emph{âtash bâzi}) — \textquotedblleft{}fireworks\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{نیمه} \fa{شب} \fa{آتش} \fa{بازی} \fa{شروع} \fa{شد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Nime shab âtash bâzi shoru' shod.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
At midnight the fireworks began.
\end{quote}

Literally \textquotedblleft{}fire play\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{âtash} \textquotedblleft{}fire\textquotedblright{} is inherited from Middle Persian (EtymDB), and \emph{bâzi} \textquotedblleft{}play, game\textquotedblright{} is native Persian too: fire play.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{رژه} (rezhe)}{رژه (rezhe)}]{\fa{رژه} (rezhe) — a parade, a march-past}

\label{lesson:FA-C342-rezhe}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for festive lights, then the Persian for fireworks.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{رژه}}
\textbf{\fa{رژه}} (\emph{rezhe}) — \textquotedblleft{}a parade, a march-past\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{روز} \fa{جشن} \fa{رژه} \fa{از} \fa{جلوی} \fa{خانه} \fa{ما} \fa{رد} \fa{شد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Ruz-e jashn rezhe az jelo-ye khâne-ye mâ radd shod.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
On the day of the celebration the parade passed our house.
\end{quote}

Written with \fa{ژ}. \emph{Rezhe raftan} \textquotedblleft{}to march in a parade\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
The origin of \emph{rezhe} \textquotedblleft{}a parade\textquotedblright{} is not settled, and EtymDB lists no entry.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{شادی} (shâdi)}{شادی (shâdi)}]{\fa{شادی} (shâdi) — joy, happiness}

\label{lesson:FA-C342-shadi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for fireworks, then the Persian for a parade.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{شادی}}
\textbf{\fa{شادی}} (\emph{shâdi}) — \textquotedblleft{}joy, happiness\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{مردم} \fa{از} \fa{شادی} \fa{فریاد} \fa{میزدند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Mardom az shâdi faryâd mizadand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
People were shouting for joy.
\end{quote}

From \emph{shâd} \textquotedblleft{}glad\textquotedblright{}. \emph{Shâdi kardan} is \textquotedblleft{}to rejoice\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{shâdi} adds the noun suffix \emph{-i} to \emph{shâd} \textquotedblleft{}glad\textquotedblright{}, a native Persian word. EtymDB lists it without a parent.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
